I am 65 years old, and I have farmed my 16.1 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years. I finished primary school, so I can read fertilizer bags and do my own calculations. My wife and I work the land together, and we have a well, so we can pump water when the rain does not come.

My main system is wheat-maize on 8 mu. I plant improved wheat seed in October and harvest in early June. Last year I used 16 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu for the wheat, and that worked, so I will do the same this year. I irrigate four times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Right after wheat harvest, I rotary-till and plant hybrid maize seed. I only have a few days, so I cannot plough deep. For maize, I put 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, at the big trumpet stage and at flowering. Summer rain sometimes helps, but those two waterings are necessary.

I keep 4 mu of peanut. Peanut needs potassium and calcium. I use 5 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, at flowering and when the pods are filling. I spray three times for leaf spot and insects. The peanut price was decent last year, so I did not cut the area.

Cotton is on 2 mu. It is a lot of work for an old man, but I keep a small plot because the price can be good. I plough the cotton field in spring. I use 13 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times and spray four times for bollworm. If you skip a spray on cotton, the bollworm will eat everything.

Millet is 1.5 mu. I grow it mainly for our own food, and I sell the extra. I put 8 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. Millet does not drink much water, so one irrigation is enough. I spray twice if the insects come.

Mung bean is only 0.6 mu, a small plot near the house. I put 3 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 2 kg potassium per mu. One irrigation and one spray for aphids is all it needs.

I hire a machine for tillage now. At 65, I cannot handle the plow like I did when I was young, but I still do the spraying and irrigating myself. I expect wheat to give me 520 kg per mu, maize 620 kg, peanut 320 kg, cotton 270 kg of seed cotton, millet 280 kg, and mung bean 110 kg. These are the numbers I usually get if the weather is normal.

I do not change much from year to year. I watch my neighbors, especially Lao Zhang. If he tries something new and it works on his field, I might try it the next year on a small piece. But I do not take big risks. Fertilizer costs real money, but losing the crop costs everything. I would rather put a little too much than be short. Every yuan counts when there are only two of us working.
